bank_name: PLACEHOLDER - Taiwan Composite Bank (identity not confirmed)
bank_name_note: Unlike BANK010 (Bradesco), this source dataset does not name a specific institution - the original academic paper (Yeh & Lien, 2009, 'Default of Credit Card Clients') anonymizes the source bank. Do not treat 'PLACEHOLDER - Taiwan Composite Bank' as a real bank name in any user-facing report - this needs an explicit decision (generic placeholder name vs. a different resolution) before actual onboarding runs.
source_description: 30,000-row revolving-credit-card-account dataset (UCI 'Default of Credit Card Clients', Yeh & Lien 2009). One row per account: credit limit, 4 demographic fields, 6 months of monthly repayment-status/bill/payment history, and a real binary outcome column (target). No loan-amount field in the installment-loan sense (this is revolving credit, not a term loan), no income field, no bureau score, no occupation/geography fields.
profiling_method: Direct read of sample datasets/Taiwan_UCI_Credit_Card.csv (30,000 rows) via pandas: dtypes, null counts, value_counts() on categoricals, target balance - confirmed 0 nulls across all 24 columns before any mapping decision below.

mappings.notes: Real labeled outcome, 0% missing, base rate 22.1%.

mappings.formula: Rank EDUCATION's categories (1=grad school, 2=university, 3=high school, 4=other, plus undocumented codes 0/5/6 present in the raw data) by their OWN observed target rate within this file, ascending risk, assign 1..N - same convention used for BANK010.
mappings.notes: Compute the risk order on the TRAINING SPLIT ONLY, not the full 30,000-row file before splitting - BANK010's onboarding script computed this on the full file pre-split, which mildly leaks test-set outcome information into the encoding. Do not repeat that mistake here.

mappings.formula: credit_limit_usd = LIMIT_BAL / fx_rate_twd_per_usd, where fx_rate_twd_per_usd comes from country_macro.TWN.fx_rate_per_usd (to be seeded)
mappings.notes: New generic canonical field, not Taiwan-specific naming (see add_taiwan_columns.py docstring) - genuine borrower attribute (credit line size), distinct from `exposure` (a live assessment-time input, not a stored training feature).

mappings.formula: repay_status_m1 = PAY_0 (most recent month; PAY_0 is the source CSV's own naming quirk - there is no PAY_1 in the original file)
mappings.notes: Values -1=pay duly, 1-9=months delinquent. Codes 0 and -2 also appear in the raw data and are UNDOCUMENTED in the original UCI dataset description - a known data-quality issue with this specific file, not an artifact of this mapping. Kept as-is (not remapped/guessed), flagged here for whoever trains on this field.

mappings.formula: repay_status_m2 = PAY_2, repay_status_m3 = PAY_3, ..., repay_status_m6 = PAY_6 (re-numbered into a clean m1..m6 sequence, most-recent-first)

mappings.notes: 0% missing, clean. Some negative values present in the raw data (overpayment/credit balance) - genuine, not an error, left as-is.

mappings.formula: Rank MARRIAGE's categories (1=married, 2=single, 3=other, plus undocumented code 0) by observed target rate, ascending risk, assign 1..N.
mappings.notes: COMPLIANCE FLAG: column is populated per 'don't lose information upfront', but must NOT be added to ml_models/trainer.py's FEATURE_COLS without an explicit review of whether marital status is an acceptable model input in this jurisdiction. Not wired into training by this mapping file.

COMPLIANCE FLAG - STRONGER THAN MARRIAGE: gender is a protected characteristic under fair-lending law in most jurisdictions (e.g. ECOA in the US). Column populated for completeness only. This field must NEVER be added to FEATURE_COLS without an explicit, documented compliance/legal review - treat as excluded-by-default, not merely unreviewed.

derived_fields.formula: 1 if any of repay_status_m1..m6 > 0 (any delay in the 6-month window), else 0
derived_fields.notes: Maps onto an EXISTING canonical field, computed from real observed repayment history - not fabricated.

derived_fields.formula: count of months among repay_status_m1..m6 where value > 0
derived_fields.notes: Maps onto an EXISTING canonical field, but the field name says '12m' and this window is genuinely only 6 months - document this honestly wherever the field is used for this bank, do not silently relabel a 6-month count as a 12-month one.

derived_fields.formula: bill_amt_m1 / credit_limit (guard divide-by-zero: NULL if credit_limit is 0)
derived_fields.notes: New derived field on the new generic schema. Standard, well-established credit-risk signal - real ratio from real data, not fabricated.

derived_fields.formula: average(payment_amt_mN / bill_amt_mN for N in 1..6, skipping months where bill_amt_mN <= 0)
derived_fields.notes: New derived field. PAY_AMT* columns showed real feature importance in dry-run testing of this dataset - worth carrying through as a summary ratio.

not_mapped_no_target_field_note: Every one of the 23 source columns + target was mapped, derived, or explicitly compliance-flagged above - this dataset has no columns that were simply skipped without a documented reason, unlike BANK010's PAK.csv which had ~24 fields with genuinely no platform-side target.
unmapped_required_fields_note: No income, occupation, geography, housing-tenure, or bureau-score fields exist in this dataset at all - it's revolving-credit billing/repayment behavior data, structurally thinner on borrower demographics than either the Utopian banks or BANK010's PAK.csv, but richer on payment-behavior history than either. Macro fields come from country_macro via country_code=TWN, once seeded (not from this file).

proposed_new_fields.proposed_fields: credit_limit, repay_status_m1..m6, bill_amt_m1..m6, payment_amt_m1..m6, marital_status_enc, gender_enc, credit_utilization_ratio, payment_coverage_ratio
proposed_new_fields.rationale: Per explicit decision: bring in all raw columns under generic, reusable names rather than collapsing to a handful of summary stats upfront, so a future per-bank multi-model comparison workflow has full raw granularity available, not just a pre-curated subset.
proposed_new_fields.status: Schema added via operations/scripts/add_taiwan_columns.py (23 new columns, all NULL on existing rows, verified). Data population NOT yet run - this file documents the mapping only.

currency_conversion: LIMIT_BAL/BILL_AMT*/PAY_AMT* are NT$ (New Taiwan Dollar). Requires country_macro.TWN.fx_rate_per_usd to be seeded (Taiwan is not yet in the countries/country_macro tables - this needs the same seeding step BRA got before Bradesco onboarding). Real Earth's canonical monetary unit is USD, same convention as BANK010.
onboarding_scope_decision: NOT YET DECIDED - open question, not resolved by this mapping file. Unlike PAK.csv (no loan-amount field at all, forcing training-only), this dataset's LIMIT_BAL is a genuine facility-size field, so a broader-than-training-only scope is plausible here. Needs an explicit decision before any onboarding script is written or run.
bank_identity_decision: NOT YET DECIDED - see bank_name_note above. Needs resolution before onboarding.
feature_cols_decision: NOT YET DONE - ml_models/trainer.py's FEATURE_COLS is still the fixed 37-field canonical list. For a single-bank training run to actually use these new columns, trainer.py needs the auto-discovery enhancement discussed separately (bank-scoped runs should use canonical FEATURE_COLS + that bank's own populated non-canonical columns, not just the fixed list). Not implemented by this mapping file or the schema migration - schema and training logic are two separate pieces of work.
world_assignment: Real Earth ('real'), same quarantine rules as BANK010 - never pooled into combined Utopian Earth training, never selectable in the Utopian Earth world view. Whether it can ever be pooled WITH BANK010 specifically is a separate, later decision requiring genuine categorical alignment work between the two Real Earth banks.
